errors.english: This mind, truly quickened, is a friend to joys.
errors.why: The line continues the epithets of the king (the friend of joys who makes the mind thrill, the earth's nectar-rayed moon); the mind is the object, not the subject that is the friend of joys.

note: A sound rendering of the king's lament; the opening epithet line is misconstrued and the 'transferred' torment is flattened, but the verses are otherwise faithful.

errors.english: Whatever the nature of the object and the subject may be
errors.why: In this argument about whether a universal pervades space, yul / yul can are place (deśa) and what occupies the place, not object and subject; the error runs through the page ('resides in its object', 'non-objects').

fix.find: Whatever the nature of the object and the subject may be
fix.replace: Whatever the relation of location and what is located may be

errors.english: The establishment of whether things are proven to be separate or non-separate is based on the relationships of (samyoga) conjunction or contact and (samavaya) inherence
errors.why: The Tibetan says that between things established as separate and as inseparable (yutasiddha/ayutasiddha) the relations are conjunction and inherence respectively; the English inverts the dependence.

In this list of conditions of perceptibility the word (with an edition note) stands for being obstructed/screened (chod pa, vyavahita), not worship; 'offering or respect' makes no sense in the argument.

note: The logical skeleton is followed, but the key term for place is rendered as object/subject throughout and several clauses of the Vaiśeṣika argument are garbled.

errors.english: controller of itself and the other
errors.why: dbang here means 'in terms of': the first of the three constructions is by way of identity and otherness, not a 'controller'.

fix.find: controller of itself and the other
fix.replace: in terms of identity and otherness

note: A careful, scholarly rendering of the commentary and the fivefold question; one mistranslated phrase in the threefold classification.

errors.english: Absorbed in the union of the two empowerments of joy
errors.why: dbang gnyis in this union context are the two organs (vajra and lotus) joined in bliss, not two empowerments.

errors.english: the joy of engaging in medicine for sentient beings
errors.why: sman pa here is 'benefit' (hita): it delights in engaging in benefiting beings, not medicine.

note: The deity description and verses are rendered faithfully overall, with two technical words misread.

errors.english: the nature is formless and unseen
errors.why: The Hevajra line says that by nature there is no form and no seer (draṣṭā); 'unseen' loses the denial of the perceiving subject.

note: A clear and largely accurate rendering of the Hevajra commentary, including the Laṅkāvatāra verse; the stray 'continues to next page' is editorial noise.

errors.english: a certain sign that the Bodhisattvas are entering into faultlessness
errors.why: skyon med pa here is the bodhisattva's niyāma (the 'flawless' certainty of the path), and the sign is that they will certainly enter it; 'certain' belongs to the entry, not to the sign.

note: A faithful rendering of the commentary on light, rays and the miracles; only the niyāma term is blurred.

errors.english: one apprehends the Truth of Cessation
errors.why: In the physician simile the Tathāgata points out the truth of cessation to the yogin; it is not the practitioner who apprehends it.
The second of the thirteen is cessation by exhaustion (zad pa, as taken up below as ཟད་པས་འགོག་པ), not 'by activity'.

errors.english: though that cessation cannot be described in any other way
errors.why: This is the first of the four (cessation cannot be said to be other than the path), followed on the next side by not-other, both, neither; it is not a concessive remark.

note: The four truths and the classification of cessation are well handled; a few items in the thirteenfold list and the tetralemma are misread.
Faithful rendering of the chapter colophon and the commentary on the perfection of non-existence, equality and seclusion.

errors.why: The king's question ends 'by what deed does he go about on a golden elephant?', which the English drops, losing the point of the story told next (the wooden elephant).

fix.replace: Through what karma, Venerable One, does he go about on a golden elephant?

errors.english: together with his monks, traveled through the world out of compassion.
errors.why: The Tibetan says once that Vipaśyin wandered in Bandhumat's city out of love for the world; the English renders it twice, once from the Sanskrit line.

note: Good rendering of the avadāna verses; the golden elephant in the king's question is lost.
A faithful rendering of the thread-laying rite and mandala measurements, with accurate direction glosses.
